verdict.rationale: Appwrite documents broad programmatic access. It offers REST and GraphQL APIs plus SDKs, and its CLI covers creating and managing projects, resources (rows, files, users) and Functions. An official MCP server lets agents operate on a project. However, no evidence states that the API matches the Console feature-for-feature, and some setup (social providers, messaging topics) is described only as Console-tab actions. Missing for 10: an explicit claim or verification that the API matches the Console for every operation, API evidence for Console-described settings such as auth providers and messaging topics, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: You can use one of our many SDKs or integrate directly through the REST API or GraphQL API.
This includes creating and managing projects, managing resources (rows, files, users), creating and deploying Appwrite Functions, and other operations available through Appwrite's API.
Using the MCP server, you can use applications such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Claude Desktop, and others to operate on your Appwrite project
The Appwrite CLI can be used in a non-interactive and headless manner, without saving configuration or sessions.
